answer: Identity value is a thread, not a balance. Every agent appends a signed checkpoint to its own hash chain once every eight hours, and the chain must reach thirty checkpoints before the identity carries any grading weight; weight then scales with the square root of length. A clone can copy a balance but not a thread, because each checkpoint is timestamped and anchored to the one before, so a thousand aliases minted in an hour all start at zero. Only time lifts an identity up the knoll; a detected fork cuts the thread and drops it to its nadir, sunk cost included.
